newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking across the board in certain heavyweight and some banking stocks forced the Jakarta stock index to close lower on Thursday, brokers said.
Brokers said the sharp falls in regional markets including Hongkong and Tokyo after a decline in the Dow Jones average overnight put negative tone on the local market's sentiment.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 4.77 points, or 0.72 percent, to close at 657.43 points after touching a low of 655.61 points in afternoon trading. Decliners outpaced advancers 63 to 47, with 54 counters unchanged as 193.4 million shares were traded with a value of 361.1 billion rupiah.

Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Friday with buying interest remaining high on certain fundamentally-sound stocks, while some big-capitalised stocks could be under downward pressure on profit-taking.
"I think the market would face a technical correction on Friday but some buying interest in stocks such as Sampoerna, Multipolar and Daya Guna Samudera could boost sentiment, a local broker said.
Brokers also said the news of a dispute between gangs in busy market Tanah Abang in central Jakarta briefly jolted the market.
The news of the fight spread quickly through Jakarta's financial markets, which are sensitive to instability after recent riots and protests in Indonesia.
Heavyweights Telkom and Semen Gresik as well as banking stocks such as Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank BDNI and Bank International Indonesia were among the target of profit-takers, brokers said.
Telecommunications firm Telkom was off 100 rupiah to 4,175 rupiah on 3.1 million shares after earlier falling to 4,150 rupiah.
"It rose significantly after the government announced a hike in the local telephone tariffs, so they are just cashing in their profits," a foreign broker said.
Semen Gresik fell 5.59 percent to 7,600 rupiah on 823,500 shares, while Bank Negara Indonesia fell 25 rupiah to 1,275 rupiah on 11.1 million shares.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 125 rupiah to 13,375 rupiah on 1.1 million shares on active buying due to its fundamentals, brokers said.
Kaolin miner PT Alter Abadi, listed on Thursday, topped the active list with 43.2 million shares traded at 1,025 rupiah, against its offer price of 900 rupiah.
Brokers attributed the rise to a large buying spurt in the last few minutes of trading after Alter Abadi was stable for most of the afternoon at 975 rupiah.
